claims.claim: In a 30-programmer mixed-methods study, highlighting tokens by predicted likelihood of being edited speeds task completion and targeted edits; highlighting by generation probability gives no benefit over no highlighting.
claims.stance_target: token-probability uncertainty is not enough for code
claims.scope_conditions: 30 participants, Python, three LeetCode tasks, Codex completions
claims.quoted_support: highlighting tokens according to their probability of being generated does not provide any benefit over the baseline with no highlighting.

claims.claim: Participants preferred highlights granular enough to narrow in on specific areas, informing granularity of uncertainty display.
claims.quoted_support: participants prefer highlights that are sufficiently granular to allow them to narrow in

claims.claim: The edit model was built from 9 participants editing completions; a token's edit probability is the fraction of participants who edited it; tokens edited by at least 4 of 6 were highlighted (203 characters).
claims.quoted_support: For each token in the completion, we then set the probability of an edit to be the fraction of participants who edited it.

breadth.confidence_families: Token generation probability from the code model versus a human-edit-likelihood model (Section 3-4).
breadth.model_families_and_sizes: OpenAI Codex (Code Davinci 002; completions retrieved June 2022) (Section on tasks).
breadth.elicitation_formats: Token-level highlights from generation probability or edit model; single completion per task (Section 4).
breadth.benchmarks: Three LeetCode-style tasks with imperfect Codex completions; no standard benchmark.
breadth.label_source: Human edits by programmers (closed-world edit model); not execution ground truth.
breadth.label_independence: Separate nine-participant data collection for the edit model vs 30-participant main study.
breadth.contamination_split: Acknowledged: training data of Code Davinci 002 undisclosed; no evidence of memorization in selected generations (Footnote 5).
breadth.calibration_metrics: not present (searched: ECE, Brier, AUROC; outcomes are task time, edits, subjective preference)
breadth.causal_intervention: Between-condition user-study intervention (highlighting conditions), not model-internal.
